title: Camera-elevation labels (~47-65°, 'pucks ≈65° STEEPEST') contradict the committed puck pad 1.15
evidence:
tools/gen_sprites.py:190-192: """ORTHO camera, the MM top-down tilt. Elevation above horizontal =
    atan(9.9 / (0.35 + 4.5*pad)) — pad 0.95 (pucks) => ~65deg STEEP (nearest
    top-down); pad 1.95 (campus) => ~47deg SHALLOW (most oblique). Any camera" — but SPRITE_SPECS pins "puck_1": ("puck", 1.15, "tier_4", None) with comment "puck pad 0.95 -> 1.15". The docstring formula on the committed pads gives: pucks atan(9.9/5.525)=60.8°, house (pad 1.12)=61.4° (actual steepest), campus 47.3°. _pr_body.md:19 claims "measured in Blender: elevation 47.3° (campus, shallowest) … 65.0° (pucks, steepest)".
detail: The W4 'tilt labels corrected' fold went stale when W5 bumped the puck pad 0.95→1.15 in the same PR: real range is ~47.3–61.4° and HOUSE is steepest, not pucks at 65°.
recommended_fix: Re-measure from the committed pads and relabel (~47–61°, house steepest, pucks ≈61°) in the gen_sprites.py docstrings, README camera row, spec §0, and PR body.

title: README references a workbench camera `wb_camera(pad)` that exists nowhere
evidence: assets/blender/README.md:39: "(`wb_camera(pad)`) IS what the pipeline renders — same aim math." — repo-wide grep finds no wb_camera; inspection of all six .blend files shows zero camera objects (root objects are only outline/roof/gable + the puck tier collections).
detail: wb_camera was an ephemeral Blender-MCP-session helper; a reader following the README cannot find it anywhere in the repo or the committed .blend sources.
recommended_fix: Drop the name (or mark it as the MCP-session helper) so the README references only committed artifacts.

title: Unused `import math` left in gen_sprites.py after the fold-in rewrite
evidence: tools/gen_sprites.py:70: "import math" — grep counts 0 occurrences of 'math.' in the file (the rewrite deleted the trig users in build_puck/add_flat_disc; only mathutils is used, 2 refs).
detail: Dead import left behind by the rewrite; every other import (bpy, os, sys, json, mathutils) is used.

title: sprite_guard.py / test_sprite_foldin.py docstrings say 'lint gate 7' but lint.sh wires it as gate 7b
evidence: tools/sprite_guard.py:5: "sprite, and tools/test_sprite_foldin.py proves the legs bite (lint gate 7)." / tools/test_sprite_foldin.py:3: "(no Blender needed — CI has none). Wired into lint gate 7." vs tools/lint.sh:92: "echo "-- gate 7b: sprite fold-in pins (W5 bbox guard bites; SPEC table consistent)""
detail: Gate 7 is test_sprite_order; the foldin test is gate 7b. The off-by-one label misdirects anyone tracing which gate runs the W5 proof.
